Report Card: Heritage and History

By: Sasha Schwendenwein | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Has Joburg City and National Department of Arts and Culture kept their promises they made in our last story? We give them a report card

Unique Selling Point:
James Ball says: Within heritage circles – lots of talk since our story – people very happy we did story – but things work very very slowly.
James says his sources are not hopeful that things will happen quickly at museumAfrica – nothing solid, but no real change.
JAG had an opening – exhibitions going again, in terms of long term restoration work though, still going through the processes – no major updates.
Hector pieterson museum open? Yes.

Jacque Stoltz says:
Speak with Flo – museumAfrica – she has been leading calls for something to be done.
At a specific site level – not much has changed.
MuseumAfrica: nothing, have appointed a curator – new staff – whether its sufficient is debatable
Jag: has reopened, but im not sure yet what status is of project to do restoration work…
Hector Pieterson Museum: open? Yes.
With the heritage association of south Africa (voluntary org) –At botshabelo – the restoration of church has happened.
At Vredefort – don’t think anything has changed…
A friend of Jacques posted on facebook – the old artefacts from tulamelo (gold kingdoms in kruger) site has disappeared. Artefact went missing – thinks ditsong is responsible.

Graeme Addison: Sent an email – waiting to hear back about Vredefort.

I have sent an email to department of arts and culture
I have sent an email to joburg city

G said that it may not be necessary now for this Sunday, but if we need this done, I’m sure we could get Vince to quickly do it tomorrow.

Press Release:


Report Card: Museums
Neglected, crumbling and broken - that was the state of some of the buildings and artefacts in many of our Museums and Heritage Sites. This week, our Report Card
returns to find out whether the officials responsible have fixed the problems in our dilapidating historical sites.

Script:


IN APRIL, WE VISITED 15 SITES OF HISTORICAL SIGNIFICANCE, TO ESTABLISH WHETHER WE ARE PROTECTING OUR HISTORY. SOME HERITAGE BUILDINGS LIKE NELSON MANDELA’S HOUSE ON VILAKAZI STREET, WERE EXCELLENT, WHILE OTHERS, LIKE THE BUILDING THAT HOUSES THE JOHANNESBURG ART GALLERY, WERE IN NEED OF RENOVATIONS.
WE ALSO VISITED SEVERAL MUSEUMS, LIKE AT CONSTITUTION HILL, WHICH HAD WELL-PRESERVED EXHIBITS, WHILE MUSEUM AFRICA, IN NEW TOWN, HAD EMPTY DISPLAY CASES, AND A LACK OF STAFF. JACQUES STOLTZ CO-FOUNDER OF THE HERITAGE MONITORING PROJECT, SAID THE SITUATION WAS DESPERATE.
OLD STORY: Jacques: “If we don’t have proper heritage management in place, a lot of that history corrodes.”
WE BROUGHT OUR FINDINGS TO THE ATTENTION OF THE NATIONAL DEPARTMENT’S ACTING ARTS AND CULTURE DIRECTOR-GENERAL, VUSITHEMBA NDIMA.
OLD STORY: Bongani: “You’ve got these expensive buildings that are hard to maintain, and the more they’re allowed to deteriorate, the more money it’s going to cost to get them to a state of repair?
Ndima: “I do agree, but also, understand one thing, some of these buildings are very old…it’s not going to be there forever…”
Bongani: “Wow, it’s not going to be there forever, that’s our best answer to that?”
Ndima: “It’s not the best answer, but I’m just being realistic.”
IT WAS CLEAR GOVERNMENT HAD FAILED TO PROTECT OUR HERITAGE. SO, WE RE-VISITED SOME OF THE SITES TO GIVE THOSE RESPONSIBLE A REPORT CARD.
FIRST UP, WE WENT BACK TO THE JOHANNESBURG ART GALLERY, WHICH FALLS UNDER THE JURISDICTION OF THE CITY OF JOHANNESBURG. THE CITY’S MMC FOR COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT NONHLANHLA SIFUMBA WAS UNAVAILABLE FOR AN INTERVIEW, BUT, THE CITY SAID THEY WOULD BE HAPPY TO ACCOMMODATE AN INTERVIEW IN A FEW WEEKS.
AS THE CITY PROMISED, JAG HAS REOPENED, BUT THE CRACKS IN THE CEILING ARE DEFINITELY VISIBLE AND THE ROOF IS STILL IN NEED OF REPAIR. FLO BIRD, CHAIR OF THE JOBURG HERITAGE FOUNDATION, SAYS THERE HAVE BEEN IMPROVEMENTS.
FLO BIRD: “It’s only reopened in part, and to be honest, I think it’s a pity, I think they should close it and bite the bullet and get on with doing a proper job.
Jacques: “I would rate the city’s efforts to address the conservation challenges at JAG a 5.”
SO a, D… FOR REOPENING IT…NEXT WE WENT BACK TO MUSEUM AFRICA.
Flo: “Where it has been good and I must give the mayor credit for this, because he found the money, the sprinklers are working which is great. They have actually upped security, they’ve got new cameras.”
THE CITY ALSO PROMISED TO ADD STAFF.
Flo: “They’ve got 11 curatorial posts, which is certainly inadequate, but better than what the position was, one chief curator and one curator, they now have no chief curator and 7 curators.”
BUT WE SAW THE DISPLAY CASES ARE STILL EMPTY.
Jacques: “Museum Africa, definitely I would continue to rate it an abysmal one or two. It’s been years now.”
SO FOR MUSEUM AFRICA, DESPITE FLO’S POSITIVE’S, JACQUES IS RIGHT, THAT IT’S BEEN TOO LONG, AND WE FOUND NO CHANGES. SO AN F.
THAT MEANS GIVE THE CITY OF JOHANNESBURG A DISAPPOINTING E.
NEXT, WE WENT BACK TO THE NATIONAL DEPARTMENT OF ARTS AND CULTURE. BUT, ASTONISHINGLY!!! THEIR CHIEF OF COMMUNICATIONS TOLD US THEIR EMAILS WERE NOT WORKING, AND THEY WOULD NOT BE ABLE TO RESPOND TO OUR QUESTIONS, AS THEY WOULD REQUIRE INPUT FROM THE DIFFERENT UNITS RESPONSIBLE.
Jacques: “We are being ignored, and our complaints are being ignored.”
SO FOR THEIR LACK OF ACTION – WE GAVE THEM A FAIL. OVERALL IT’S CLEAR OUR HERITAGE IS NOT A PRIORITY.
